newsitem.title: USA: Hecla to complete La Choya mining Q1 1998.
newsitem.headline: Hecla to complete La Choya mining Q1 1998.

text.p: Hecla Mining Co said Thursday that after four good years of operation, mining is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 1998 at its La Choya gold mines in Mexico.

It said that La Choya produced 39,175 ounces of gold in the first half of 1997 at an average cash cost of $184 per ounce. Processing of heaps at the mines is expected to continue through at least the end of next year, Hecla said.
On other developments, Hecla said per ounce production costs are expected to decrease at its Greens Creek silver/zinc/gold/lead mine in Alaska as ore grade improves throughout the year.

Greens Creek, a joint venture with Kennecott Greens Creek Mining Co, a unit of Rio Tinto Plc, has produced 1,383,793 ounces of silver for Hecla's account so far this year, at an average cash cost of $2.32 per ounce, it said.
The mine's cash costs per ounce also include credits from by-product metals, so Greens Creek benefitted from the higher price of zinc during the second quarter of this year, it said.
It said early third quarter mining results indicate ore grades in the range of 30 ounces of silver per ton, compared with about 24 ounces per ton in the first six months of 1997.
